title: Trivial ell-adic condensed coefficients: the coordinate-cup exterior complex
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. For $F=E,\Omega$ put $A_F(S)=C(S,F)$, using all continuous maps on profinite sets [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Let $r\geq0$, let $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ with its inverse-limit topology, and give $A_F$ the trivial condensed $L$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Write $C_F(L)=R\Gamma_{A_F,L}(A_F[0])$ for ordinary internal-module derived invariants [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $1\le i\le r$, the coordinate inclusion $a_i:L\to(F,+)$ sends $(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ to $x_i$ under $\mathbf Z_\ell\subset\mathbf Q_\ell\subset F$. Let $\alpha_i:A_F[-1]\to C_F(L)$ be its connecting character class, and use the unital derived cup product of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus].

Define $\mathcal E_{A_F,r}$ to be the complex with zero differential and term $\bigoplus_{|I|=q}A_F$ in degree $q$, for $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and $0\le q\le r$, zero in all other degrees. Equivalently it is $\bigoplus_I A_F[-|I|]$. Define a morphism
$$\chi_{F,r}:\mathcal E_{A_F,r}\longrightarrow C_F(L)$$
by the unit on the empty-subset summand and by $\alpha_{i_1}\smile\cdots\smile\alpha_{i_q}$ on the summand $A_F[-q]$ for $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}$. This specified morphism is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_F})$. For $r=0$ it is the identity $A_F[0]$. The assertion concerns all-continuous $\Omega$ with its norm topology, not its completion or a filtered-union topology.

source.place: Paragraph (3), dense-lattice input: trivial-representation analytic base case, coordinate-cup derived exterior calculation. Exact all-continuous noncomplete-coefficient reference WANTED.

proof.text: Put $A=A_F$. Use the polynomial complex $P_{A,r}$ specified in [lem-sfb-polynomial-derived-bar-comparison]. Its term in degree $n$ is the internal direct sum of $A$ on the monomials in $nr$ variables; its differential is polynomial substitution and addition. The cochain map $i:\mathcal E_{A,r}\to P_{A,r}$ of [lem-sfb-rational-polynomial-bar-contraction] sends the summand for $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}$ to $x_{1,i_1}\cdots x_{q,i_q}$, and the empty summand to $1$. Here its complex $K_{A,r}$ is exactly the based zero-differential complex $\mathcal E_{A,r}$ in our statement.

source.place: Paragraph (3), trivial-representation analytic base case; agent polynomial-bar reduction, step 1

proof.text: Extend the rational maps $p,h$ of [lem-sfb-rational-polynomial-bar-contraction] internally to $A$. On a polynomial with coefficient $c\in A(S)$, apply the finite rational matrix on monomials and multiply the resulting rational coefficients by $c$. Every image of a basis monomial is a finite sum, so these are morphisms from the internal direct sums and require no infinite sums in $F$. The formulas commute with every restriction $S'\to S$ and with multiplication by sections of $A$. The identities $pi=1$ and $dh+hd=1-ip$ hold on every monomial with every section coefficient, hence hold as internal maps. Thus $i$ is already a chain homotopy equivalence of internal complexes. Its inverse in the derived category is $p$, since the displayed homotopy identifies $ip$ with the identity. This step uses a universal rational contraction, not an exactness claim for scalar extension.

source.place: Paragraph (3), trivial-representation analytic base case; agent polynomial-bar reduction, step 2

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-polynomial-derived-bar-comparison] to precisely the norm-topological field $F$ and the profinite lattice $L$ of the statement. It gives the isomorphism $\eta_{F,r}:P_{A,r}\to\mathscr B_A(L)$. All polynomial evaluations use the prescribed inclusions $\mathbf Z_\ell\subset\mathbf Q_\ell\subset F$. Combining with the equivalence $i$ just proved gives an isomorphism $\eta_{F,r}i:\mathcal E_{A,r}\to\mathscr B_A(L)$. In particular this step retains the higher internal-Hom resolutions: no column of the derived bar is asserted to be underived, and no convergence in a completion is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), trivial-representation analytic base case; agent polynomial-bar reduction, step 3

proof.text: The group $L$ is profinite, the coefficient $A$ is commutative, and it has the specified trivial action. Therefore [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar], with $N=A$, supplies the normalized augmentation isomorphism $\epsilon:C_F(L)\to\mathscr B_A(L)$. Define $\theta=\epsilon^{-1}\eta_{F,r}i$. Each factor is an isomorphism, so $\theta:\mathcal E_{A,r}\to C_F(L)$ is an isomorphism. All internal modules, injective resolutions and profinite powers are taken in the coefficient universes in the cited statements.

source.place: Paragraph (3), trivial-representation analytic base case; agent polynomial-bar reduction, step 4

proof.text: For $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}$, polynomial evaluation sends $i(e_I)$ to the cochain $(g_1,\ldots,g_q)\mapsto a_{i_1}(g_1)\cdots a_{i_q}(g_q)$, and $\eta_{F,r}$ is evaluation followed by the canonical underived-to-derived map $j$. By [lem-sfb-internal-bar-ordered-cup], applied to $G=L$ and the ordered list $a_{i_1},\ldots,a_{i_q}$, its map into $\mathscr B_A(L)$ is $\varepsilon_q\,\epsilon\circ(\alpha_{i_1}\smile\cdots\smile\alpha_{i_q})$, with the connecting-class normalization and derived cup of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] and a sign $\varepsilon_q=\pm1$ depending only on $q$. The same lemma with $q=0$ sends the empty monomial to $\epsilon$ composed with the unit, and $\varepsilon_0=1$. Compose these equalities with $\epsilon^{-1}$: $\theta$ agrees with $\varepsilon_{|I|}\chi_{F,r}$ on the summand of $I$. Let $\sigma$ be the automorphism of $\mathcal E_{A,r}$ multiplying the summand of $I$ by $\varepsilon_{|I|}$; it is its own inverse. Maps out of this finite direct sum are determined by their composites with its summand inclusions, so $\theta=\chi_{F,r}\circ\sigma$. Hence $\chi_{F,r}=\theta\circ\sigma$ is an isomorphism, being a composite of isomorphisms. This proves the assertion for the actual ordered-cup arrow, with no appeal to equality of its cohomology maps alone, and is independent of the shift sign convention.

source.place: Paragraph (3), trivial-representation analytic base case; agent polynomial-bar reduction, step 5

proof.text: If $r=0$, $L$ is the one-element group. Every action is forced to be trivial by its identity law, so its invariant-submodule functor and its invariant inclusion are the identity. This functor is exact, so its ordinary derived value on $A[0]$ is $A[0]$ and its unit is the identity. The complex $\mathcal E_{A,0}$ has just the empty-subset summand $A[0]$, whose map is that unit. Hence $\chi_{F,0}=1_{A[0]}$, as asserted. Both choices of $F$ were treated using the same polynomial formulas and the same norm-topological comparison.
